notice: Short summaries of NASA and CSA material. The links to metrics were chosen by the AstroCheck team; they are not diagnostic rules of the agencies and not astronaut measurements.

sources.title: Why do we conduct science experiments in space?

entries.title: Circulation in weightlessness
entries.summary: Weightlessness changes how the heart, blood vessels and circulation work.
entries.projectUse: We show heart rate and blood pressure together with their history to follow changes.
entries.limitation: These measurements do not identify the cause of changes and do not diagnose the effects of weightlessness.

entries.title: Sleep and irregular schedules
entries.sourceSection: Risk of Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
entries.summary: Sleep loss and disrupted biological rhythms are among the risks under study.
entries.projectUse: Sleep duration is part of the daily entry and the charts.
entries.limitation: Duration does not describe sleep quality; the BE-08 threshold comes from a separate terrestrial source, not NASA.

entries.title: Fitness, bones and muscles
entries.sourceSection: Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness
entries.summary: NASA studies exercise to preserve physical fitness in flight.
entries.projectUse: We show activity and back-pain reports as context for a discussion with a medic.
entries.limitation: Exercise minutes and pain do not measure bone density or muscle strength. The pain scale is a team choice.

entries.title: Eye and brain changes
entries.sourceSection: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
entries.summary: Spaceflight can be accompanied by changes in the structure of the eyes and the brain.
entries.projectUse: We added a diary of subjective blurred vision.
entries.limitation: A self-rating does not diagnose SANS and does not replace an eye examination.

entries.title: Lack of oxygen
entries.summary: NASA studies the risk of hypoxia in preparation for spacewalks.
entries.projectUse: SpO₂ can be recorded and its trend reviewed.
entries.limitation: A pulse oximeter does not identify the cause of a deviation. The prototype has no automatic SpO₂ rule.

entries.title: Immune response changes
entries.sourceSection: Risk of Altered Immune System Responses
entries.summary: Spaceflight stressors can affect the immune system.
entries.projectUse: Temperature is included as a general self-monitoring metric.
entries.limitation: Temperature does not measure the immune response and does not confirm an infection.

entries.title: ARCHeR: sleep, activity and well-being
entries.summary: The study tracked the well-being, activity and sleep of the Artemis II crew.
entries.projectUse: We grouped these metrics into daily observation.
entries.limitation: Our self-reports do not reproduce the ARCHeR protocol or instruments; the mood scale was designed by the team.

entries.title: Standard Measures: consistent observations
entries.summary: The study collects a consistent set of physiological and psychological measurements.
entries.projectUse: We use repeated records with units, times and provenance.
entries.limitation: This is how our app is organised, not an implementation of a NASA research protocol.

entries.title: Radiation: a separate instrument channel
entries.summary: CSA describes the development of CANS, an autonomous instrument for continuous measurement of neutron exposure in space.
entries.projectUse: We show the limit of the monitoring: radiation needs its own measurement channel. Heart rate, blood pressure and well-being do not replace it.
entries.limitation: AstroCheck has no dosimeter and no radiation channel. We do not receive CANS data, do not calculate dose and do not assess radiation safety.

entries.title: Weightlessness, physical activity and the heart
entries.sourceSection: Using the knowledge obtained to improve our quality of life on Earth
entries.summary: CSA explains how studies of the body in weightlessness help to understand the effects of reduced physical activity; the heart, blood vessels and bones are among the subjects.
entries.projectUse: We link the activity diary with heart-rate and blood-pressure observation: you can open the history or record a new measurement. This is the team's choice for organising observations.
entries.limitation: The CSA overview sets no heart-rate or blood-pressure thresholds and no exercise norms. Our records do not reproduce the research protocol and do not prove the effect of weightlessness on a specific measurement.
